Definition: Adin, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Adin is the head of a family that came back from exile — 454 of his sons in Ezra's list — and one of his descendants, Ebed, came up with Ezra himself. His name also appears among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no teaching hidden in this name, and I won't invent one. Its value is the record it keeps: whole families came home, signed their names to the covenant, and belonged again to God's people after the exile.
RelatedTopics: Exile and Return; Return from exile; Covenant renewal
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
